title: 2026 UK ETS cross-boundary CCS current-rule QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines
UK ETS: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines (accessible webpage)

facts.source_fact: Pipeline transport of greenhouse gases intended for geological storage is currently a regulated UK ETS activity.
facts.expected_handling: Keep current-rule status distinct from consultation proposals.

facts.source_fact: CCS pipeline operators currently require UK ETS permits.
facts.expected_handling: Do not convert current permit duty into a proposed simplification.

facts.source_fact: EA regulates relevant installations in England.
OPRED delivers Secretary of State functions for specified offshore CCS areas including the UK continental shelf.
NRW, SEPA and NIEA regulate their respective devolved jurisdictions and territorial seas as described.
Under existing rules responsibility transfers at relevant regulatory boundaries.
A separate permit is required from each relevant regulator under the existing cross-boundary arrangement.
facts.expected_handling: Do not present consultation single-permit options as current law.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring infrastructure is currently required to determine CO2 transferred at regulatory boundaries.
A territorial-sea to UK continental-shelf transfer can occur at sea.
The consultation was issued to consider simplification and does not itself implement the proposed options.
